messages.subject: Structure, FSTAT, GENETIX and Genepop formatted file example
parts:
Dear Zhian,

I would like to import the formatted file like Structure, FSTAT, GENETIX and Genepop, but I don't know what these files look like. Do you have any such files examples that I can have a loo like Monpop.csv(GenAIEx file format)? 

Furthermore, in your example, you can just use read.genalex() to import Monpop file, but in my coding (provided by others) I need to use three files to get really working, one is GenAIEx file, one ispop file and one is config file wih information of ploidy, rep.length and file.sep. I attached all three files and would like to hear the working methodology inside. If I want to import other formatted file like Structure, should I also need such 3 files?

Hope to hear from you and learn something new.

Thank you very much.

Best regards
Ying

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Structure, FSTAT, GENETIX and Genepop formatted file example
parts:
Hello Ying,

You can find examples of these files in adegenet: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/tree/master/inst/files
That being said, if you are using code provided by others, I'm afraid that I can't be of much help because I'm not sure what assumptions they made.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Structure, FSTAT, GENETIX and Genepop formatted file example
parts:
Hello Ying,

The last time I had to look up these particular file formats was probably 8 years ago (I was just starting out as a grad student); I don't really remember how to find the spec for these formats anymore, but I would recommend looking at the website for PGDSpider, which is a java utility to convert to and from different genetic file formats: http://www.cmpg.unibe.ch/software/PGDSpider/#Input_and_output_formats You will find links to the different softwares, where hopefully you can find definitions of the format. 

For what it's worth, I know that STRUCTURE is particularly difficult because it can optionally encode individuals on one or two rows. 

I hope that helps.

Best,
Zhian
